title: The two-row Schubert coefficient bound conjecture
statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group of permutations on $[n]$. For $w\text{ in }S_n$, let $\mathfrak{S}_w$ be its Schubert polynomial. Let $lambda$ be the two-row Young diagram corresponding to a $k$-Grassmannian permutation $tau$ in $S_{n_1}$, and let $s_{lambda}(x_1,dots,x_k)$ be the associated Schur polynomial. For a permutation $w$ in $S_{n_2}$, define the generalized Littlewood–Richardson coefficients by

$$
\mathfrak{S}_{w}s_{lambda}(x_1,dots,x_k)=sum_{vin S_n}c_{wtau}^{v}\mathfrak{S}_{v},qquad n=max{n_1,n_2}.
$$

**Two-row Schubert coefficient bound conjecture.** For every $vin S_n$,

$$
0leq c_{wtau}^{v}leq n_2-k.
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform linear upper bound for generalized Littlewood–Richardson coefficients when the Schur factor corresponds to a two-row Young diagram. The preceding results establish sharper bounds in several cases, including coefficients in ${0,1}$ or ${0,1,2}$ for $k$ close to $n_2$, but the general bound remains open in the supplied text.
source_name: Zijie Tao and Yunchi Zheng, “Bounds On Schubert Coefficients in the Two-Row Case”, arXiv:2411.19735 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19735

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).
